subject.title: [Bug]: IRC channel reports healthy while dead-looping reconnects on a non-recoverable login error

question: For IRC post-ready reconnects that fail with fatal login codes `432`, `464`, or `465`, should OpenClaw mark the account terminally failed, or keep retrying with capped backoff while publishing `connected: false` and `lastError`?
rationale: The source-backed bug is real, but the permanent-fail versus capped-retry behavior determines operator recovery semantics and should not be guessed by automation.

options.title: Capped Retry With Honest Status
options.body: Publish `connected: false` plus the reconnect error immediately, use bounded exponential backoff, and allow recovery if the server-side IRC condition is fixed.

options.title: Terminal Fatal Failure
options.body: Treat these reconnect login codes as terminal for the account, stop retrying, and require an explicit operator restart after fixing credentials or bans.

options.title: Status-Only First Slice
options.body: Land only the disconnected/error status propagation first, leaving retry policy unchanged until a later explicit channel-health decision.

recommendation.title: Capped Retry With Honest Status
recommendation.body: Publish `connected: false` plus the reconnect error immediately, use bounded exponential backoff, and allow recovery if the server-side IRC condition is fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans IRC plugin behavior and shared gateway health policy, and this handle appears in recent history for both implicated surfaces.
